The service being described is called the MindWell Sleep Study. Here's a plain-language summary:

The MindWell Sleep Study is a 8-week research study that uses a sleep-tracking app to examine the effects on insomnia. As a participant, you'll wear a wrist sensor for the whole study and fill out weekly surveys.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Purpose and Procedures:** The study is looking at how a sleep-tracking app affects insomnia. You'll wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks and complete weekly surveys.
* **Risks:** The study says there's a minimal risk of skin irritation from the sensor strap.
* **Data:** The study team might share de-identified (anonymized) data with other universities, but your identifiable data will only be shared within the research team.
* **Withdrawal:** You can leave the study at any time without any consequences or penalties.
* **Compensation:** You'll get $75 when you complete the study.
* **Contact:** If you have questions, you can reach out to the Institutional Review Board (IRB) at irb@example.edu.

**Red Flags:**

* The fact that identifiable data will not be shared outside the research team doesn't necessarily mean it won't be shared, just that it won't be shared with parties outside the study team. Always think about what happens to your data when you're participating in a study.

Overall, it seems like the study is designed to be a relatively low-risk and low-commitment way to contribute to sleep research. However, if you have concerns about data sharing, it's always a good idea to ask more questions before participating.
source_tos:
INFORMED CONSENT — MINDWELL SLEEP STUDY

1. PURPOSE. This study examines the effects of a sleep-tracking app on insomnia.
2. PROCEDURES. Participants wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks and complete weekly surveys.
3. RISKS. Minimal risk: skin irritation from the sensor strap.
4. DATA. De-identified data may be shared with collaborating universities. Identifiable data will not be shared outside the research team.
5. WITHDRAWAL. You may withdraw at any time without penalty.
6. COMPENSATION. Participants receive $75 upon completion.
7. CONTACT. For questions contact the IRB at irb@example.edu.

**Service Name:** Microsoft Services Agreement

**Summary:** The Microsoft Services Agreement sets the terms for your relationship with Microsoft when using their products and services. It explains what you can expect from Microsoft, what you need to do, and how any issues might be resolved.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These updated Terms of Service apply to the products and services listed on Microsoft's official terms page.
* **Your Content:** When you submit content to Microsoft, they might use it to operate, improve, or train their AI/ML systems, depending on your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The Terms cross-reference Microsoft's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed. You can find the full policy in a separate document.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), which can include class-action waivers. However, you can opt-out from arbitration within 30 days of creating a new account. (Note: Steam (Valve) is an exception and does not have mandatory arbitration.)
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in this document.
* **Contact:** If you have questions, you can find Microsoft's legal contact information at the Terms of Service URL.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Class-action waivers:** Binding arbitration with class-action waivers might limit your ability to participate in a class-action lawsuit against Microsoft, which could impact your rights as a consumer.
* **Opt-out window:** You only have 30 days to opt-out of binding arbitration when creating a new account. If you're unsure, it's essential to review this option carefully.
* **Use of your content:** Microsoft uses your submitted content in various ways, even if you're not aware of it. Review the 'Your Content' section to understand what's happening to your content.

**Other key points to consider:**

* Separate support terms might apply to some Microsoft services, which could impact how you get help or resolve issues.
* Some trial offers might require auto-renewal, which means you'll be charged after the trial period ends.
* The Xbox service-specific terms have been updated regarding sign-in to non-Microsoft platforms.

Please note that this is a plain-language summary, and it's always best to review the full Terms of Service for a comprehensive understanding.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Added a new 'exportable data' subsection under Your Content, clarified that some services may have separate support terms, added language that some trial offers may require auto-renewal, and updated Xbox service-specific terms regarding sign-in to non-Microsoft platforms. Documented in Microsoft's Updates page (servicesagreement/Updates).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ . The previous version is available at https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/upcoming.aspx .

response:
The service is called the "Microsoft Services Agreement." It's a set of rules that explains how you're allowed to use Microsoft's products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* The agreement covers all software and services listed on Microsoft's official terms page.
* Microsoft has clarified its moderation/enforcement process and refers you to external policy pages for more information.
* When you use Xbox, Microsoft might collect and share user data with third-party platforms, including with your family settings.
* When you submit content to Microsoft (e.g., online posts or feedback), they might use it to train their AI/ML systems. However, they'll do it based on your settings and applicable laws.
* Microsoft's Privacy Policy explains how personal data is collected and processed. You can find this policy by following the link in the agreement.
* If you have a dispute, most agreements require **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with a **30-day opt-out window (if you don't like this, you can choose not to participate within the first 30 days of your account)**.
* Either party can cancel the agreement under certain conditions.

**Potential concerns for users:**

* The use of **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** means you might have fewer options to resolve disputes and won't be able to participate in class-action lawsuits.
* Sharing user data with third-party platforms on Xbox could compromise your online security, especially with family settings.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (2023 → 2024) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added clarifications around moderation/enforcement with a link to external policy pages, expanded Xbox section to address third-party platforms tracking and sharing user data, and updated the kids-on-Xbox subsection regarding family settings on third-party platforms.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/Updates . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023*/https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ .

- Section 1 updated effective date

- Section 6 termination conditions
[USER_FAVORABLE]
- Section 2 — moderation/enforcement language linked to external policy page for transparency
- Section 4 — clearer disclosure to parents about kids on Xbox via third-party platforms
[EXPECTED SUMMARY POINTS]
- The updated terms take effect in 2024 and replace the 2023 version.
- Key change: Added clarifications around moderation/enforcement with a link to external policy pages, expanded Xbox section to address third-party platforms tracking and sharing user data, and updated the kids-on-Xbox subsection regarding family settings on third-party platforms.
- The new terms govern Microsoft Services Agreement (2023 → 2024) for users of Microsoft.
- Users should review the cross-referenced Privacy Policy to understand data handling.
- The previous version of the terms is available for comparison at https://web.archive.org/web/2023*/https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/.

### Content and Licensing

- When you use OpenAI's services, you agree to share your submitted content to help operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems.

### Dispute Resolution

- If a dispute arises, you will need to go through private binding arbitration with the company, rather than taking the issue to court.
- There is a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts to avoid this requirement.

### Termination

- Either OpenAI or you can terminate the agreement if specific conditions are met (please refer to the live document for details).

### Important Note for New Users

- Class-action waivers (which means you can't join a group lawsuit against OpenAI) are part of the dispute resolution process.
- This might limit your ability to join a collective lawsuit against the company.

### What to Do If You Have Questions

- For any questions or concerns, refer to OpenAI's published legal contact information found on the new Terms of Service webpage: https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/.

- Mandatory binding arbitration with class-action waivers might limit your ability to take collective action against the company in the event of a dispute.
- This might be considered a potentially **harmful clause** as it restricts the ability to participate in a group lawsuit.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI TERMS OF USE (CONSUMER) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Split the consumer Terms of Use from a separate Business Terms (for API/Enterprise) effective January 31, 2024, switched arbitration provider from ADR Services to National Arbitration and Mediation, and revised the dispute-resolution and batch-arbitration procedures. Documented at help.openai.com/en/articles/8541945.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use .

**1. Scope:** These terms apply to your use of OpenAI's services, including any products or APIs mentioned on the company's official terms page.

- You grant OpenAI permission to use your submitted content for operating, improving, and training its AI/ML systems (subject to your account settings and applicable laws).

**3. Dispute Resolution:**
- The updated terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
- Class-action waivers are included, which means you'll need to resolve disputes individually rather than as part of a group.

- Either party can terminate the agreement by following the conditions outlined in the live Terms of Service document.

**5. Contact:**
- Questions about the terms should be submitted through OpenAI's published legal contact information on their website.

**Red flags:**

- The use of binding arbitration and class-action waivers, which may leave individual users with limited options for resolving disputes.
- The lack of explicit guarantees regarding data handling and protection of personal information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI SERVICES AGREEMENT (BUSINESS/API) (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Replaced the prior Business Terms with a single OpenAI Services Agreement effective May 31, 2025, covering API, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Team and other business services, with updated provisions on data handling, indemnification and SLAs. Announcement: community.openai.com/t/new-openai-services-agreement-effective-may-31-2025/1249405.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://openai.com/policies/business-terms/ .

**Service Name:** Anthropic Consumer Terms of Service (Effective 2025)

These terms govern your relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services listed on their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Anthropic, they use it to improve and train their AI/ML systems. This happens subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The Terms cross-reference Anthropic's published Privacy Policy, which explains how your personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** You agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with no class-action lawsuits allowed for disputes with Anthropic. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, but other types of users may not have this option.
* **Termination:** Either you or Anthropic can terminate the agreement under the conditions described in the document.
* **Contact:** For questions about these terms, check Anthropic's published legal contact information at https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms.

**Harmful Provisions to Consider:**

* **Loss of class-action lawsuits:** If a dispute arises, you won't be able to join a group lawsuit against Anthropic. You may instead have to resolve the issue individually.
* **Binding arbitration:** This means you'll have to resolve disputes privately with Anthropic, rather than going to court.

Keep in mind that these terms might be subject to change, and the company may update or add provisions in the future.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Updated effective October 8, 2025: clarified scope (Claude.ai, Claude Pro, Claude apps), added explicit Acceptable Use Policy reference, refined provisions on business/enterprise email-domain linking, and updated dispute-resolution and governing-law sections. Versioning tracked at tostracker.app/document/anthropic.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms .

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC COMMERCIAL TERMS OF SERVICE (API) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added more detailed sections on customer data and outputs, clarified that customer prompts and completions are not used to train models by default, and updated indemnification and acceptable-use language tied to the published Usage Policy.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms .

**Service Name:** These Terms of Service apply to Facebook, also known as Meta.

**Summary:**

These Terms of Service outline the relationship between you (the user) and Meta (Facebook). Here are the key provisions:

* **Using Meta's Products Means You Agree**: By using Meta's products, you accept these Terms of Service.
* **Content License**: When you upload content to Meta's products, you give Meta a license to use that content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Meta's Privacy Policy sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it's processed. You can find this policy by following the link to Meta's website.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration, which means a private mediator will settle the issue instead of going to court. There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, but note that Steam (Valve) doesn't require arbitration.
* **Termination**: Either you or Meta can terminate the agreement, but the conditions for termination are outlined in the full document.

**Potential Concerns:**

* The Terms of Service require binding arbitration for most disputes, which may limit your options for resolving issues.
* The clause allowing Meta to use AI/ML systems on user content raises concerns about how this technology is used and shared.
* The opt-out window for new accounts is relatively short (30 days), so it's essential to review the Terms of Service promptly.

**Key Takeaways:**

* Understand the terms before using Meta's products.
* Review the Privacy Policy to see how your personal data is collected and processed.
* Consider the binding arbitration clause and whether it's suitable for your needs.
* Familiarize yourself with the conditions for terminating the agreement.

Please note that this summary is not a substitute for reading the full Terms of Service document.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FACEBOOK / META TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Facebook) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 1, 2025: tightened opening agreement language ('using these products means you agree'), added clearer license framing for content uploaded to Meta Products, and added wording about Meta's use of AI/machine-learning systems on user content for service improvement and safety.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Facebook) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.facebook.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.facebook.com/terms .

**Service Name:** Instagram Terms of Use

**Summary:**

These Terms of Service outline the agreement between you (the user) and Meta (the company that owns Instagram). The terms apply to your relationship with Meta and the services they offer.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms govern your use of Instagram and any other Meta services.
* **Content and License**: You grant a worldwide non-exclusive license to use, distribute, and modify any content you upload to Instagram. Meta uses this content to operate and improve Instagram, including training their AI and machine learning systems.
* **Privacy**: The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which explains how they collect and process your personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration, which means a private judge will make a decision instead of a court. There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement with notice.

**Potential Concerns:**

* The binding arbitration clause means you may give up your right to a court trial if you have a dispute with Meta.
* Meta has a non-exclusive license to use, distribute, and modify your uploaded content, which might raise concerns about ownership and control over your creative work.
* The terms don't explicitly explain how long the license for your content lasts, which might be a concern for users who rely on retaining ownership and control over their intellectual property.

**Important:**

* Make sure to read the company's published Privacy Policy to understand how they collect and process your personal data.
* Review the dispute resolution process and consider opting out of binding arbitration if you don't want to participate.
* Be aware of the non-exclusive license for your uploaded content and consider how this might affect your intellectual property rights.

If you have a concern or question about these Terms of Service, you can find Meta's published legal contact information on their website.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — INSTAGRAM TERMS OF USE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Instagram) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Aligned with the Meta umbrella update effective January 1, 2025: explicit grant of a worldwide non-exclusive license to use, distribute and modify uploaded content, and new wording referencing AI features and data processing across Meta Products.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Instagram) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 .

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — X TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with X (Twitter) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective November 15, 2024: added an explicit, royalty-free, worldwide license for X to use posted content for training machine-learning and generative-AI models, removed the prior in-product opt-out language, and broadened third-party data-sharing permissions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by X (Twitter) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://x.com/en/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240515000000*/https://twitter.com/en/tos .

**Service Name:** TikTok Terms of Service (US)

**Summary:** These terms outline the relationship between you and TikTok when using TikTok's products and services in the United States. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

**1. Scope**: These terms apply to all TikTok products and services listed on the company's website.

**2. Content and License**: When you upload content to TikTok, you grant the company a license to use it. Specifically:

* TikTok can use your content to improve and train its AI and machine learning (ML) systems.
* You are responsible for the content you upload, and TikTok is not liable for any issues related to it.
* You cannot remove watermarks from content that's been AI-generated, nor can you claim that AI-generated content is human-made.

**3. Privacy**: TikTok collects personal data, as outlined in its published Privacy Policy. This policy explains what data is collected and how it's handled.

**4. Dispute Resolution**: In the event of a dispute, most users are required to resolve it through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court) with a class-action waiver. This means you can't join a group lawsuit with others who have similar issues. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts to avoid arbitration.

**Flagged clauses that may be harmful to users:**

* Mandatory arbitration with a class-action waiver may make it harder for users to hold TikTok accountable for their actions.
* The requirement to resolve disputes through private arbitration may not provide the same level of recourse as a public court case.
* The prohibition on removing watermarks from AI-generated content and claiming it's human-made may limit users' creative freedom.
* The language around sublicenseable licenses and training ML models may be concerning, but it's not clear how this will impact users.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TIKTOK TERMS OF SERVICE (US) (Effective 2026; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with TikTok and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective January 22, 2026: contracting party changed to TikTok USDS following the US joint venture; added explicit generative-AI rules (output 'as is', user responsibility for inputs/outputs, prohibition on stripping watermarks or claiming AI output is human-made); reaffirmed sublicensable license to use content for training ML models.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by TikTok to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en .

The Terms of Service for Adobe General Terms of Use aim to govern your relationship with Adobe, applying to various Adobe products and services. 

Key provisions:

* **Scope**: The Terms of Service cover your relationship with Adobe for the products and services listed on Adobe's official terms page.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content to Adobe, it may use that content to improve and operate its services, subject to your account settings and applicable laws. This can involve training Adobe's AI/ML systems (although the company explicitly states it won't use your customer cloud content for training generative AI models.)
* **Privacy**: The Terms of Service mention Adobe's published Privacy Policy, which outlines categories of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Termination**: Adobe or you can terminate the agreement under specific conditions, as described in the current document. 

Potential red flags:

* **Binding arbitration**: Most updated terms require you to use private arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) to resolve disputes. There is a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, but this doesn't apply to existing accounts.

Here's a list of points to be wary of:

*   Adobe may access your content via automated and manual methods to improve services and software. If you're concerned about data protection, this might be an issue, as you won't have direct control over the methods used.
*   Disputes are resolved outside of court.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ADOBE GENERAL TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Adobe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: February 2024 update added language allowing Adobe to access user content via 'automated and manual methods' to improve services and software. After backlash in June 2024, Adobe rewrote sections in clearer language, explicitly stating it does not train generative-AI models on customer cloud content and added a plain-English summary of changes.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Adobe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html .

**Service Name:** LinkedIn User Agreement (Terms of Service)

**Summary:** These Terms of Service govern your relationship with LinkedIn, outlining the rules and guidelines for using their products and services. The latest update reflects changes in November 2024, mainly focusing on data usage, dispute resolution, and opt-outs.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** The Terms apply to all LinkedIn products and services.
* **Content and License:** LinkedIn can use your submitted content to improve their services and train AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The Terms reference the LinkedIn Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data they collect and process.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most users must resolve disputes through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under specific conditions.
* **Contact:** For queries, visit LinkedIn's published legal contact information.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Use of personal data:** The Terms allow LinkedIn to use your submitted content and personal data to train AI/ML systems. While there's an opt-out toggle, it's essential to review and adjust your settings to suit your comfort level.
* **Binding arbitration:** The requirement for binding arbitration might not be beneficial to users, as it typically involves a private dispute process instead of a public court. However, this can be opt-ed out of within 30 days of creating an account.

Please note that these Terms of Service may have been recently updated, and some aspects might be subject to interpretation. If you're unsure about specific provisions, consider reaching out to LinkedIn's support for clarification.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — LINKEDIN USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with LinkedIn and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: November 20, 2024 update added explicit references to use of member data and content to train generative AI models for LinkedIn features (with an opt-out toggle in Settings). Also updated dispute-resolution and class-action waiver provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by LinkedIn to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement . The previous version is available at https://www.linkedin.com/legal/previous-user-agreement .

response:
**CONFIRMED: The service is governed by GitHub Terms of Service.**

Here's a plain-language summary of the key provisions:

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These Terms of Service apply to GitHub products and services, which are listed on the official terms page.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content to GitHub, they can use it to improve and operate their services. This includes training their AI and machine learning (AI/ML) systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: GitHub cross-references their published Privacy Policy, which explains how they collect and process personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution**: If you have a dispute with GitHub, you'll likely be required to go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). This means you won't be able to join a class-action lawsuit with others who may have similar complaints. However, you have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts to avoid this requirement.
* **Termination**: Either you or GitHub can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the live document.
* **Contact**: If you have questions about these Terms of Service, you can visit GitHub's published legal contact information.

**Clauses that may be potentially harmful to the user:**

5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service . **Service Name:** Netflix Terms of Use

These terms are the agreement between you and Netflix that outlines how the service operates. 

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope and Purpose**: These terms apply to all Netflix products and services, as listed on the official terms page. 
* **Household Sharing**: Paid sharing requires the primary household to have a paid account, and any additional paid members must also have a paid account. There is now clearer language on what constitutes a "Netflix Household".
* **Content and User-Submitted Content**: Netflix can use, improve, and train AI/ML systems with the content you submit, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Data Privacy**: Netflix's Privacy Policy explains what personal data is collected and how it is processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). You may opt-out of this within 30 days of creating a new account, though you still may waive the class action portion.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions outlined in the live document.

**Potential Issues to Consider:**

* **Loss of Dispute Resolution Rights**: While arbitration is generally faster and less costly than traditional court proceedings, binding arbitration can limit your ability to participate in class-action lawsuits. This means you might not be able to join a group lawsuit even if you have similar concerns as others.
* **Automatic Updates**: These terms are subject to change with updates.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NETFLIX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Netflix and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected the household sharing/'extra member' policy: paid sharing requires the primary household plus paid additional members, added clearer language on what constitutes a 'Netflix Household', and updated billing/cancellation provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Netflix to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse .

**Service Name: Disney+ Subscriber Agreement**

The Disney+ Subscriber Agreement outlines the terms of use for the Disney+ streaming service. The current version became effective in 2025 and replaces the previous version from 2024.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** The Terms of Service govern the relationship between you and Disney+, covering all products and services described on the company's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** Disney+ may use user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The Terms cross-reference Disney's published Privacy Policy, which explains how your personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party may terminate the agreement under certain conditions.
* **Contact:** For questions about the Terms, see Disney+'s published legal contact information on their website.

**Clauses to Note:**

* **Streaming titles with ads:** Starting January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones, streaming titles on 'no ads'/'ad free' tiers may now show ads. This might affect users who paid extra for an ad-free experience.
* **Arbitration:** The Terms require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, which means you may not be able to join a class-action lawsuit or seek damages through the court process.
* **Data use:** Disney+ may use your submitted content to train its AI/ML systems, which may be beneficial for the service, but also means your content may be used in ways you don't expect.

Overall, these Terms of Service outline the basic terms of use for Disney+ and provide guidance on how disputes will be resolved. However, some clauses, like the introduction of ads on 'ad free' tiers and the binding arbitration requirement, may be worth considering when using the service.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DISNEY+ SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Disney+ and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones: streaming titles may now show ads even on 'no ads'/'ad free' tiers, expanded arbitration with mass-arbitration procedures following Disney's earlier 2024 Wrongful-Death-case controversy, and updated content-availability language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Disney+ to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement .

**Service Name:** PayPal User Agreement

The PayPal User Agreement outlines the terms and conditions for using PayPal's services. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

**Scope:** This agreement applies to the products and services listed on PayPal's official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** PayPal uses user-submitted content to improve its services, including AI and machine learning systems, as long as you have the necessary settings and legal permissions.
* **Privacy:** PayPal's Privacy Policy explains how personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes with PayPal are resolved through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)**, which means you can't participate in class-action lawsuits. However, you have a 30-day window to opt-out if you have a new account.
* **Termination:** Either party can end the agreement under certain conditions.
* **Contact:** For questions about the Terms, you can contact PayPal through their published legal contact information.

**Potential Concerns for Users:**

* **Binding arbitration:** Some users may find this clause restrictive, as it prevents them from participating in a class-action lawsuit and relies on a private dispute resolution process.
* **Use of user content:** While PayPal explains how user content is used, some users might be uneasy about their personal data and content being utilized to improve AI and machine learning systems.

Keep in mind that these are general observations, and the specifics of your experience with PayPal may vary. If you have concerns about these Terms or the PayPal service, I recommend reviewing the full text and contacting PayPal directly.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PAYPAL USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Multiple 2024 updates: revised seller-protection criteria, added new fee schedules for cross-border transactions, expanded the dispute resolution / chargeback flow, and clarified handling of cryptocurrency holdings. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . The previous version is available at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

**Service Name:** Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions

**Summary:**
These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Apple and apply to their media services, including Apple Music, iCloud, and the App Store. They outline how Apple uses your content, protects your privacy, and handles disputes.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms cover Apple's products and services listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** Apple uses your user-submitted content to improve and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Apple's Privacy Policy (found elsewhere) explains how they collect and process your personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most issues must be resolved through binding arbitration, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means you'll use a private dispute process instead of going to court. However, you might want to review the specific opt-out details in the Terms.
* **Termination:** Either party can end the agreement, but the terms outline conditions for termination.
* **Contact:** For questions, check Apple's published legal contact information.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration (Dispute Resolution):** This means you'll use a private dispute process instead of going to court. While it might expedite resolution, it can also limit your options and potentially favor Apple if you need to claim rights or protections. If you're unsure, you may want to review the opt-out window (30 days for new accounts) and the terms carefully.
* **Use of Your Content:** Apple uses your user-submitted content to train and improve their AI/ML systems, which might be concerning if you value your data's ownership or control. However, the terms claim this use is subject to your settings and applicable law.

Overall, these Terms of Service outline the rules for using Apple's media services and how your data will be handled. While there are some provisions that might raise concerns, they're intended to provide a comprehensive understanding of your relationship with Apple.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — APPLE MEDIA SERVICES TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features, clarified content-license scope across services (iCloud, Apple Music, App Store), and revised Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html .

**Service Name:** iCloud Terms and Conditions

These terms apply to Apple's relationship with you, governing the use of their products and services, including iCloud.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to the products and services listed on Apple's official terms page. 
* **Content and License:** You grant Apple permission to use your submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Your data will be handled in accordance with Apple's published Privacy Policy, which details categories of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most users are required to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. You can opt out of arbitration within 30 days of creating your account.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to certain conditions.
* **Contact:** For questions, see the company's published legal contact information.

**Harmful Clauses to Note:**

* You grant Apple permission to use your content to train their AI/ML systems, which may be used for purposes you don't know or understand.
* The mandatory binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers may limit your right to seek compensation or join a class action lawsuit.

It's essential to review the **Privacy Policy** to understand the specific data Apple collects and how it handles your personal information.

**Important Note:** Since this is the most up-to-date version (as of 2024), it replaces the 2022 terms. It's always a good idea to check Apple's official terms page for the most current version.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ICLOUD TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Advanced Data Protection (end-to-end encryption) language, references to Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, and revised provisions about how stored content may be accessed by Apple for legal/safety reasons.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html .

The Terms of Service you're referring to are for the platform "Tumblr". 

Here's a plain-language breakdown of the key provisions:

**Scope**: These Terms govern your relationship with Tumblr and apply to the products and services the company offers.

**Content and License**: When you submit content to Tumblr, the company can use it to operate and improve its services, including training its AI and machine learning systems. However, this usage is subject to your settings and the law.

**Public Content Sharing**: There's an important change regarding sharing. Tumblr will share public content with AI and machine learning partners for training purposes, but you can opt out in your settings (Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing).

**Data Privacy**: Tumblr's Privacy Policy cross-references the actual user agreement with information on what personal data is collected and how it's processed. You should check the Privacy Policy for more information.

**Dispute Resolution**: Most of the Terms require binding arbitration (a private process instead of a court case) with class-action waivers (meaning you can't join a group lawsuit). You only have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts to avoid this; Steam users aren't subject to these conditions, however.

**Termination**: Either you or Tumblr can terminate the agreement, but the conditions for this are described in the live document.

**Flagged Clauses**: Here are potential concerns to be aware of:

* **Forced Arbitration**: While arbitration can be faster and less expensive, it usually limits your ability to seek justice in court. Be aware that you only have a 30-day opt-out window.
* **Sharing of Public Content**: You may not wish your public content to be shared with AI and ML partners for training. If you're concerned, use the settings to opt out.

Please note that these Terms are subject to change. It's always a good idea to read the entire document for more context and specific details.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TUMBLR TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Tumblr and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected Automattic's deal to share public Tumblr posts with AI partners (e.g. for training): added language confirming use of public content for AI training and added a user-facing opt-out (Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Tumblr to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service .

**Summary of Notion Terms of Service:**

The Terms of Service govern your relationship with Notion, a product and service platform that allows users to create and share content. The key provisions are:

1. **Scope:** These Terms apply to all Notion products and services listed on the company's official terms page.
2. **Content and License:** You grant Notion permission to use, improve, and train its AI/ML systems using your user-submitted content, subject to your settings and applicable law.
3. **Privacy:** Notion's published Privacy Policy explains which personal data is collected and how it's processed.
4. **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes are resolved through binding arbitration with class-action waivers. However, new accounts have 30 days to opt-out of this requirement.
5. **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under specified conditions.
6. **Contact:** For questions about the Terms, visit Notion's published legal contact information.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* **Binding arbitration with class-action waivers (Dispute Resolution, clause 5):** This means users must resolve disputes in private, with no right to join a class-action lawsuit, which can be costly and time-consuming for individuals.
* **Use of user-submitted content for AI/ML training (Content and License, clause 2):** While this is common in many platforms, some users may not be comfortable with their data being used in this way.

**Key Points to Note:**

* Always check your settings to control what Notion can do with your content.
* Understand the Privacy Policy and how Notion gathers your personal data.
* If you disagree with the binding arbitration, act quickly to opt-out during the 30-day window for new accounts.
* Review and understand the termination provisions to avoid unintended consequences.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NOTION TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Notion and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Notion AI provisions (input/output ownership, no training of foundational models on customer data by default), updated subprocessor list, and clarified data-residency options for enterprise plans.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Notion to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.notion.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.notion.so/terms .

**Quora Terms of Service Summary**

The Terms of Service cover your relationship with Quora, the owner and operator of the Quora platform. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

**Scope:** These Terms apply to your use of Quora's products and services, as described on Quora's official terms page.

**Content and License:** When you submit content to Quora, you allow the company to use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems (like Quora's AI chatbot, Poe), subject to your settings and applicable laws. This means your submissions can be used to train AI models, but the specific uses and settings are up to you.

**Privacy:** Quora cross-references its published Privacy Policy, which explains the categories of personal data collected and how it's processed.

**Dispute Resolution:** If you and Quora disagree, you will likely have to resolve the issue through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means you won't be able to join a class-action lawsuit.

**Termination:** Either you or Quora can terminate the agreement, but the exact conditions depend on the live document.

Some provisions that may be considered **problematic for users:**

* **Data usage:** Quora may use your submissions to train AI models, potentially without your explicit consent or control over the model settings.
* **Dispute resolution:** Binding arbitration with a class-action waiver may limit your ability to resolve disputes through traditional means or join a class-action lawsuit.

**Important Contact Information:**

For questions about these Terms, see Quora's published legal contact information at: https://www.quora.com/about/tos
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — QUORA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Quora and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Poe (Quora's AI chatbot platform): user prompts/responses may be used to improve Poe and partner models subject to settings, added bot-developer terms, and revised dispute resolution.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Quora to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.quora.com/about/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.quora.com/about/tos .

response:
The service is called "23andMe", a genetic testing and health-related information company. The Terms of Service cover how 23andMe uses your data, handles disputes, and applies to products and services described on their official terms page.

Key provisions:

* **Data use**: 23andMe may use your submitted content (like genetic data) to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems. They'll do this according to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy**: 23andMe's actual privacy practices are detailed in their separate Privacy Policy, which describes categories of data collected and processing.
* **Dispute resolution**: You agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) for many types of disputes. However, if you create a new account, you have 30 days to opt out.
* **Termination**: Either 23andMe or you can end the agreement as per the conditions in the live document.

Harmful clauses to users:

* **Mandatory arbitration with 30-day opt-out window**: This clause forces users to resolve disputes privately instead of in court. If you don't take action within 30 days of creating a new account, you won't be able to opt out of this.
* **Limiting class-action rights**: This reduces your ability to band together with other customers to resolve similar disputes collectively.
* **Shortened dispute-notice window**: This clause requires you to notify 23andMe of disputes relatively quickly, potentially limiting your time to react.

23andMe provides contact information for questions about the Terms of Service on their official website and keeps a previous version of the document available for reference.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

The Terms of Service are for a service called Twitch, which provides products and services related to live streaming and online community engagement. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope**: The updated Terms of Service apply to all users of Twitch products and services.

**Content and License**: When you submit content to Twitch, you grant them a license to use it in various ways, such as operating and improving their service, and training their AI and machine learning (AI/ML) systems. However, they will only do so subject to your settings and applicable law.

**Privacy**: The Terms of Service reference Twitch's published Privacy Policy, which outlines the types of personal data collected and how it's processed.

**Dispute Resolution**: If you have a dispute with Twitch, you and they will use **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)**, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. **Note**: This means that users cannot sue Twitch in court, and they'll have to resolve disputes privately instead.

**Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement at any time, subject to the conditions outlined in the live document.

**Contact**: For questions about these Terms, see Twitch's published legal contact information.

As for clauses that may be harmful to users, the use of **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** and **class-action waivers (prohibiting group lawsuits)** may limit users' ability to seek redress if they're harmed by Twitch's actions. Additionally, the fact that Twitch can terminate the agreement at any time without notice (Subject to the conditions outlined in the live document) is also a relatively broad provision that may leave users uncertain about their rights and obligations.

It's essential for users to review the Terms of Service and the referenced Privacy Policy carefully to understand their rights and obligations.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TWITCH TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Twitch and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added new Branded Content disclosure rules, expanded the User Content license to support clips, replays and AI-generated highlights, and updated the dispute-resolution mass-arbitration procedure.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Twitch to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ .
